title: PT-4403: Cover empty-chapter localize keys, announce the zero state

reviews.author: katherinejensen00
reviews.bodyText:
Review of PR #2717 — Cover empty-chapter localize keys in en/es parity tests

PR: #2717
Author: jolierabideau
Branch: pt-4403-blank-chapter-cleanup → main
Head reviewed: 65c981d86ab
Size: 4 files, +97 / −21
Reviewed: 2026-09-04

To the PR author: The extraction itself is clean and the parity gap you found is real —
Localization-Guide.md:492 lists en/es key gaps as a blocking issue, and this is the repo's first
mechanical enforcement of that rule, which is a genuinely good contribution. But the new whole-file
guard has one blocking defect: it makes the test file fail silently and totally in the exact
scenario it was written to catch. Separately, the new .const.ts module's stated reason for
existing does not reproduce, and three of the six added strings are user-visible data changes riding
under a test-shaped title.
Findings confirmed by running code are marked [verified].
Paths are relative to the repo root; the prefix extensions/src/platform-scripture-editor/ is
abbreviated as …/ after its first use.

Blocking
1. extensions/src/platform-scripture-editor/src/localized-strings.test.ts:296 — Severity: High (blocking)
Summary: A missing or renamed es block now wipes out all 181 tests in this file instead of
failing them, so the guard destroys the file's coverage at the exact moment it is supposed to fire.
The two Object.keys() calls sit in the describe callback, which runs during collection, not
inside an it. A throw there aborts the whole file. [verified] — renaming the JSON's "es"
block to "es-419":




base (main)
PR head




result
110 failed / 57 passed (167) — file collects, every test names its key
Tests: no tests — 0 of 181 collected, bare TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object at :297:25



The hazard is new to this PR: at base, every localizedStrings.en/.es read is inside an it body.
Trigger is a one-word edit in a 38 KB JSON (locale retirement, regional-variant rename, bad merge).
Fix: move both Object.keys reads inside the it bodies.

Important
2. …/src/empty-chapter-view.const.ts:5 — Severity: Medium-High
Summary: The new module's sole stated justification — that a node-environment test cannot
import the component — is false, and it has now been copy-pasted into a third file.
The header says importing the component "would drag in platform-bible-react, which touches
document at module load." [verified] — pointing the test's import at
./empty-chapter-view.component: 181/181 pass. extensions/vitest.config.ts is a single
environment: 'node' with no jsdom override and no platform-bible-react alias, so there is no
hidden rescue. Further, 66 test files under extensions/src (45 in this extension) use
// @vitest-environment jsdom, and book-not-available-view.component.test.tsx:1,6 uses that
pragma and imports its component directly.
There is a real cost (collect time 0.52s → 2.46s), which is a fine reason to keep the split —
but it is not the reason written down. A comment asserting a false invariant is worse than none,
because the next person copies it into a fourth .const.ts.
3. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:130 — Severity: Medium
Summary: This PR makes the neighbouring comment factually false, and the filter it justifies now
excludes the very key you just translated from the only assertion that would catch a regression.
The comment claims "%versionHistoryCommit_*% is en-only across the whole file." Your first hunk
gives all three Spanish values. [verified] — replacing the filter with .filter(() => true)
yields 184/184 green, so it can simply be deleted. Until then
%versionHistoryCommit_beforeRemoveCharacterMarker% has no "es differs from en" coverage
anywhere.
The comment's second clause — about the sync-blocked key — describes a key not in
REMOVE_CHARACTER_MARKER_STRING_KEYS at all; that half is pre-existing.
4. …/contributions/localizedStrings.json:241 — Severity: Medium
Summary: The three %versionHistoryCommit_*% values are not UI chrome — they are persisted,
cross-user project data, and translating them here leaves the repo shipping two contradictory
policies for one key family.
[verified] — these flow through commitVersionHistorySnapshot
(editor-side-effects.utils.ts:82-87) into
papi.commands.sendCommand('paratextBibleSendReceive.commitChanges', …), i.e. a commit message
written into version history and shared via Send/Receive. Meanwhile platform-scripture ships
33 locales and its sibling keys (_beforeReplace, _beforeReplace_failureMessage,
_afterReplace) are English-only in all 33. A Spanish translator's history then interleaves
"Antes de insertar nota al pie" with "Before doing Replace", permanently — labels freeze at
commit time.
Worth a deliberate product call, not a side effect of turning a test green.
5. …/src/empty-chapter-view.component.tsx:56 — Severity: Medium
Summary: The PR adds 12 tests about these four keys and zero that the component picks the
right one — an inverted ternary passes all of them.
No .test.tsx and no .stories.tsx exist for this component (both siblings have both). Nothing
covers isResource ? MESSAGE_RESOURCE_KEY : MESSAGE_KEY. Invert it and all 12 new tests still pass,
while an editable project shows "This chapter is empty in this resource." beside a live
Add chapter number button — exactly what the two-key split exists to prevent.
Pre-existing, but the new parity tests create false confidence that the view is covered.

Moderate
6. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:295 — Severity: Medium-Low
The guard checks key-set parity but never that es differs from en, so pasting English into es
satisfies it. [verified] — setting es['%versionHistoryCommit_beforeInsertFootnote%'] to its
English value leaves 181/181 green. That is the fastest way a future developer unblocks the new
red test. A blanket differs-check needs an allowlist ([verified] exactly 4 keys legitimately
share values, all placeholder-only format strings); at minimum, document the limitation beside the
guard.
7. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:290 — Severity: Medium-Low
The guard compares locale-to-locale and never code-to-JSON, so a key referenced in code but absent
from both locales is invisible — and those are precisely the keys the comment names as its
motivation (platform-scripture-editor.web-view.tsx:331-332, consumed at :1579/:1596). Rename
one in the JSON and the literal %versionHistoryCommit_beforeInsertFootnote% gets written into
collaborators' version history while the suite stays green.
8. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:299 — Severity: Medium-Low
it('declares every English key in Spanish') opens with the assertion for the opposite direction
(line 300 checks Spanish keys missing English values), and since expect throws, line 301 — the
direction the title describes — never runs. Split into two direction-accurate blocks.
9. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:276 — Severity: Medium-Low
%webView_platformScriptureEditor_emptyChapter_messageResource% is [verified] already covered
via model-text-panel.const.ts:34 at :228-240. The real gap was three keys, not four. This file
maintains two explicit "checked elsewhere" mechanisms (:73-84, :134) and the new block ignores
both, so one broken value now fails two suites with unrelated names.
10. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:291 — Severity: Medium-Low
The rationale comment's cited example is checkably wrong:
%versionHistoryCommit_beforeRemoveCharacterMarker% is in an exported array
(use-remove-character-marker.hook.ts:24-27). It went uncovered because of the filter at :134,
not because no array exports it. Only the two beforeInsert* keys fit the described class.
11. …/src/empty-chapter-view.const.ts:28 — Severity: Medium-Low
New TSDoc says the test "iterates every exported *_STRING_KEYS array." It iterates nine
hand-written imports; the extension exports fourteen. Your own comment at test:290-292 says the
opposite. Copied verbatim from book-not-available-view.const.ts:33-34 — fix both.
12. …/src/empty-chapter-view.component.tsx:54 — Severity: Medium-Low (accessibility, pre-existing)
Renders a bare <div><span> with no role="status", no focus target, no focus repair — unlike both
siblings doing the same swap (book-not-available-view.component.tsx:88-101,
resource-message-view.component.tsx:55-70). The editor subtree gets display:none, so a
screen-reader user arriving at a blank chapter has focus fall to <body> with nothing announced.
The return path is handled; the arrival path is not, and no comment records it as deliberate.
13. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:296 — Severity: Low-Medium
Titled "across the whole contribution file" but reads only en/es. Note: iterating all locales
would be wrong — platform-scripture deliberately ships 32 partial locales (3–11 keys each) and
the guide's fallback chain handles that by design. Fix the title, not the loop.
14. .context/standards/Localization-Guide.md:228 — Severity: Low-Medium
States "Both are required for the build to pass." [verified] false: no localization check in any
npm script or workflow, and 444 en-only keys ship today. Your own test comment (:31-32) says the
opposite. Per CLAUDE.md's "promote settled conventions," point the guide at where the guard actually
lives.

Minor / Nit
15. …/src/empty-chapter-view.const.ts:17 — Severity: Low
The four keys are hand-listed twice; Object.freeze(Object.values(EMPTY_CHAPTER_VIEW_KEYS))
preserves the literal union. Mirrors the sibling deliberately — but the sibling has a reason this
file lacks (its object feeds DISABLED_REASON_TOOLTIP_KEYS), and
resource-panel-strings.utils.ts:59 already derives. Change both files or neither.
16. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:304 — Severity: Low
A 380-key mutation sweep found no input where this it fails alone; it is subsumed by the first for
every realistic case. Collapse to one accurately-named test plus a separate non-empty-value
assertion.
17. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:300 — Severity: Low
!localizedStrings.en[key] tests truthiness where existence is meant, so an empty-string value
makes the two it blocks assert contradictory things about the same key. Object.hasOwn states the
intent.
18. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:281 — Severity: Low
The whole-file guard makes 'has a Spanish label' unfalsifiable in all seven per-key blocks (56 of
181 cases now carry no unique detection power). Note what does survive, so a later cleanup does
not delete the wrong half: 'has an English label' is the only code→JSON link, and
'Spanish differs from English' the only untranslated-copy check.
19. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:274 — Severity: Low
Seventh verbatim copy of the same three-assertion block (~94 lines across :36–:276). You
declined a helper as a pre-existing pattern — fair, but this PR is what makes the shape obsolete
rather than merely repetitive, so it is worth recording as a decision.
20. …/src/localized-strings.test.ts:295 — Severity: Low (scope)
[verified] 444 en-only keys across five extensions; this guard lands on the one file already at
190/190. A repo-scoped test globbing extensions/src/*/contributions/localizedStrings.json with a
shrink-only allowlist would ratchet the backlog instead of needing N copy-pastes.
21. .context/standards/Architecture-Decisions.md (absent entry) — Severity: Low
CLAUDE.md requires recording cross-cutting decisions. Two candidates here: the whole-file parity
convention (your own body calls the escape hatch undesigned) and the now-five-file .const.ts split
pattern.
22. Commit 65c981d86ab / PR body — Severity: Low
Missing the Session-URL: trailer and the AI-assisted — [session](url) line CLAUDE.md requires.
Matters more than usual since the body states the implementation was authored during the review
session.
23. …/src/empty-chapter-view.const.ts:2 — Severity: Nit
{@link EmptyChapterView} cannot resolve — the symbol lives in the module this file deliberately
does not import. Line 25 uses backticks for the same symbol. Identical in the sibling; fix together.
24. …/src/empty-chapter-view.component.tsx:56 — Severity: Nit (low confidence)
The message renders as an unstyled <span>; book-not-available-view.component.tsx:105-107 uses
tw:text-center tw:text-sm tw:text-muted-foreground with an explicit comment that the treatment
should match across surfaces.
25. …/contributions/localizedStrings.json:282 — Severity: Nit (latent)
"La estructura está bloqueada. Los marcadores…" would fail this file's own sentence-case rule
(test:60-66) if its scope were widened, because the rule skips only word index 0 and is not
sentence-boundary aware. Fix the rule before growing its scope, not the translation.
26. PR title — Severity: Nit
"Cover empty-chapter localize keys in en/es parity tests" understates it: three of six added values
are new user-visible Spanish strings (see finding 4). The strings themselves are correct and
consistent with in-file precedent — añadir matches the exact "No se pueden ___" construction at
:263/:265.

Verified clean

JSON hunks are pure appends with zero existing values modified (immutability rule satisfied); both
blocks stay alphabetized at 190/190.
The component's export surface is effect-identical to base, render body byte-identical, no import
cycle, no dropped export.
Lint clean on all four files; suite green at 181/181 as submitted.

Two candidate findings were refuted and dropped: the guard does not foreclose the
metadata.fallbackKey pattern, and the un-namespaced %versionHistoryCommit_*% family has no
cross-extension collision (1162 distinct en keys across 10 extensions, zero defined twice).
If you fix only one thing, make it finding 1 — it is a two-line move, and it is the difference
between a guard that reports the problem and one that hides it.

Review method
Four passes, cross-checked against each other:

Developer / soundness pass (code quality, testing, breakage risk).
Code-architect pass (pattern conformance, where the change belongs).
Comments-and-documentation pass (accuracy, density, forward-facing test).
An adversarial pass that attacked passes 1–3, followed by /code-review max with the finding cap
raised to 16 per subagent and 30 for the final report.

The adversarial pass killed six of eleven initial findings, including one graded positive that
inverted into finding 2. Every high-severity claim above was re-verified by executing it against the
PR head in a scratch copy; the review worktree was restored to a clean state afterwards — no
commits, no changes to the PR, no comments posted.
